candidates.name: Bock Casemates
candidates.reason: Anchor sight within the Wenzel Circuit. Pass B resolved conflicting secondary hours/price figures (10:00-17:00/18:00, EUR4-8 on aggregators) against the operator's own current page (see disagreement d-casemates-hours-price-conflict), but could not corroborate a specific off-peak crowd-timing claim to the >=2-independent-firsthand bar within budget -- every 'go early to avoid crowds' source found was SEO/aggregator-tier, not a dated firsthand account. No timing claim is shipped from this pass; the resolved hours/price stand as objective evidence only.

candidates.name: Mullerthal Trail
candidates.reason: The half-day-out option that best serves the party's underused nature/outdoors priority without duplicating the culture/history depth already built from the city's own fortifications and museums.

candidates.name: Vianden Castle
candidates.reason: The default half-day-trip pick, but reached only via a train-then-bus transfer (Ettelbruck, then bus 570), versus a single direct free bus to Echternach. It is also another castle/history stop layered on top of an already history-heavy city plan, rather than serving the party's third, currently thin priority (nature/outdoors). Not pursued further as the recommended half-day trip.

candidates.name: Um Dierfgen
candidates.reason: The guidebook-default address for Luxembourgish specialties in the capital. Multiple independent review sources (resto.lu, TripAdvisor listing text seen via search) consistently describe it as full and effectively needing a reservation at lunch and dinner -- the opposite of the party's stated 'eat well without booking anything formal.' Could not fetch the operator's own site to confirm or refute directly (umdierfgen.lu returned 403 on both a direct attempt and a mirror retry), so no reservation-policy evidence record is shipped for it -- but the weight of consistent secondary reports is enough to route the recommendation elsewhere.

candidates.name: Manzoku Ramen Bar
candidates.reason: Genuinely walk-in-only by design (no reservation system exists at all, virtual queue instead), matching the party's preference exactly. Important caveat: only open Wed-Sat, closed Sun-Tue -- for an Oct 16-19 (Fri-Mon) visit that leaves only Friday and Saturday inside opening hours.

candidates.name: Kaito Ramen
candidates.reason: Walk-in/first-come-first-served daily, open every day of the Oct 16-19 stay (11:30-21:30), which Manzoku is not. Corroborated as genuinely busy at midday, so best used as a lunch-just-before-noon or dinner pick rather than a peak-lunch drop-in.

candidates.name: Konrad Cafe & Bar
candidates.reason: Repeatedly mentioned as a casual, walk-in-friendly local favourite (well-known carrot cake). Only one directly-fetched firsthand source found within budget (planethibbel.com); a second independent firsthand source was not secured (a second candidate article truncated on fetch). Held as a lead, not shipped as a corroborated experiential pick.

candidates.name: Beim Siggy
candidates.reason: Clausen brasserie repeatedly recommended for Luxembourgish food with a valley view over the Grund. Could not corroborate firsthand within the two-attempt fetch budget: the one personal-blog write-up found no longer resolves (DNS failure), and TripAdvisor returned 403 on every attempt this pass (restaurant review page, forum thread, and a mirror retry). Omitted rather than shipped unverified.

candidates.name: Chiggeri
candidates.reason: Well-regarded but consistently positioned and reviewed as upscale fine dining with an extensive wine list -- the wrong register for 'eat well without booking anything formal.' Not pursued further.

evidence.claim: The Wenzel Circular Walk is a free, self-guided ~2.5km/3-hour signposted route (named for Duke Wenceslas II) that links the Bock rock/casemates, the medieval Wenzel-era fortifications, the Chemin de la Corniche and the upper and lower town -- a single route through the exact combination of fortifications and valley-adjacent walking this party asked for.
Bock Casemates: open daily (year-round except Dec 25 and Jan 1), entry every 15 minutes from 09:45 to 19:00 (last admission), maximum 45 minutes per visit; adult admission EUR11.00 (2026).

The Pfaffenthal Panoramic Elevator is free, rises 71m connecting Pescatore Park in the upper town to the Pfaffenthal district at the bottom of the Alzette valley, and runs daily 05:45-01:00 (closed for maintenance the first Monday of each month, 09:00 to 05:45 the next day) -- a practical way to walk down into the valley and ride back up rather than reclimbing.

Public transport (bus, tram, and 2nd-class train) has been free throughout the entire territory of Luxembourg since 1 March 2020, for residents and visitors alike; only 1st-class rail travel requires a paid ticket.
RGTR bus line 201 runs Luxembourg City (Limpertsberg) - Echternach directly, no transfer, free like all Luxembourg public transport.

Schiessentumpel is the busiest point on the Mullerthal Trail loop near Echternach; walking it right at opening, before the day's tour/hiking groups arrive, changes the experience -- noticeably quieter and near-empty at the falls.

Manzoku Ramen Bar takes no reservations at all (virtual waitlist queue via an app once full); open only Wednesday-Saturday (Wed-Thu 11:30-14:00, Fri 11:30-14:00 and 18:00-21:00, Sat 18:00-22:00), closed Sunday-Tuesday.
Kaito (Place de Paris location) is walk-in / first-come-first-served daily 11:30-21:30; only groups of 8 or more can book a table in advance.

Kaito's Place de Paris location gets genuinely busy at midday; since it's walk-in only (no reservations except groups of 8+), arriving by or around noon on a weekday is the practical way to get a table without a long wait.

Luxembourg has three official languages (Luxembourgish, French, German). French is the most consistently useful single language for visitors in shops, cafes and restaurants, especially in the capital; roughly 80% of the population also speaks English as a practical backup. Locals themselves switch between all three day to day: Luxembourgish for broadcast media and everyday talk, German for print, French for business and formal matters.

transport.route: Luxembourg City (Limpertsberg) to Echternach via RGTR bus line 201
transport.doorToDoor: Direct bus, no transfer, free of charge; runs roughly every 30 minutes per aggregator schedules (not independently fetched from the official timetable PDF this pass).
transport.groupLuggageMobility: Not relevant for a 2-person half-day trip with no luggage.
transport.nextService: Every ~30 minutes through the day (per mobiliteit.lu line page and third-party timetable aggregators).
transport.fallback: Lines 211/212 also connect Luxembourg City to Echternach via a longer routing through intermediate villages, per the Mullerthal Trail's own mobility page (not independently fetched by Pass B).

disagreements.topic: Bock Casemates opening hours and adult admission price
disagreements.investigation: Initial aggregator/search results gave 10:00-17:00 (18:00 in summer), open March 1-November 2 only, adult price cited as either EUR8 or EUR4. Fetching the operator's own current page (luxembourg-city.com) directly showed a different picture: open year-round except Dec 25/Jan 1, timed entries every 15 minutes from 09:45-19:00, adult EUR11.00 (2026).
disagreements.resolution: Treated the fetched operator page as the current T0 source over the older/lower secondary figures; see ev-casemates-hours-price. Does not change any recommendation, only the specific hours/price to publish.

reservations.notApplicableReason: None of Pass B's shipped/detour candidates require booking -- Manzoku and Kaito are walk-in only by design, and the Wenzel walk, Pfaffenthal elevator and Mullerthal/Echternach trip need no reservation, matching the party's explicit no-formal-booking preference.

transport.notApplicableReason: The only inter-city route Pass B evaluated (Luxembourg City-Echternach) is a direct, ~30-minute-frequency, free public bus with no transfer -- rated risk 1, well under the R3+ threshold that would require full transport-depth research.

saturation.note: The claims that cleared the >=2-independent-firsthand bar (Mullerthal/Schiessentumpel crowd timing, Kaito midday crowd) did so within the first couple of targeted searches. Later rounds chasing the remaining open items -- Casemates off-peak timing, a second Konrad source, Beim Siggy corroboration, Um Dierfgen's own site -- kept returning the same SEO/aggregator content or hit blocked origins (TripAdvisor 403 on every attempt this pass; two personal-blog domains unreachable; r.jina.ai mirror not permitted in this environment; yt-dlp not installed, so no video transcripts were attempted). None of those unresolved items are likely to flip a recommendation -- they were left as honest omissions/rejections (see candidates) rather than pursued past the point of duplicate results.

nativeLanguage.why: Luxembourg's genuine resident-angle content (personal travel blogs, culinary press, forum-style reviews) runs mostly in French and German rather than English tourist coverage; Luxembourgish itself is rarely used for this kind of written web content, so 'native-first' here meant leaning on French/German queries rather than literal Luxembourgish translations, plus a French/German-domain filter over the usual English top-10.
